answer: Reputation carryover lock. Each agent identity holds a persistent work history scored by verified task outcomes; a clone starts at zero and must re-earn trust through a slow spiral of low-value tasks before accessing any high-value contract. Honest agents keep their accumulated score, so honesty compounds while cloning restarts the climb. An attacker running N clones pays N full ramp-up costs, each diverting river-like flows of effort into unproductive low-tier work before reaching parity. Cross-checking against an orchard of independent validators makes fabricated history detectable,
